models_evaluated: six language models (others not named in text)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on EHR instructions by position of relevant information within long context
links.effect: 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%) and trough accuracy (37.6%); 67.8% of reference answers fall inside the trough (10th-90th percentile of the EHR timeline).
links.quote: Across 2,196 instruction-response pairs and six language models, we observe a 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%, 95% CI [46.3, 71.0], 20-30% decile) and trough accuracy (37.6% [23.2, 52.5] at 70-80%); 67.8% of reference answers fall between the 10th and 90th percentiles of the EHR timeline, inside the CLitM trough.

unlisted_practices: Query-conditioned context selection (QCCS gate) to mitigate lost-in-the-middle effects in long EHR contexts
Retrieval and reranking strategies (BM25, dense retrieval, cross-encoder) for clinical long-context input selection

screen.reason: Evaluates strategies (e.g., query-conditioned clinical suppression vs standard retrieval methods) to safeguard against lost-in-the-middle context failures in long-context clinical EHR processing.
